raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Since #61149 (DeepGEMM 2026-09-30), the SM100 MQA logits of the sparse indexer are BF16. Under DCP they are upcast to FP32 before the top-k, so the low 16 bits of every candidate score that reaches the DCP top-k merge are zero. The merge selector, `StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel`, radix-sorts the 64-bit key `score << 32 | ~token_id` in 11-bit passes. BF16 scores almost always tie at the top-k boundary. The radix then also walks the 16 zero score bits and the constant high bits of the token id, and each of those passes funnels every remaining candidate into a single histogram bin.

This PR packs only the bits that carry information into the key: the 16 high score bits when the logits were BF16, and the token-id bits that positions below `max_model_len` need. The selected set is unchanged.

## Claims

- Removes the DCP top-k merge cost that #61149 added. It applies to every DSA model with a sparse indexer under DCP on SM100 (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x).
  - With BF16 scores, the selector costs 1.6-1.7x what it costs with FP32 scores.
  - With this PR it is back to the FP32 cost. Per call at top-2048 on GB300:
    - DCP4: 16.7 → 10.6 us (FP32: 10.4), and 21.0 → 11.5 us on concentrated scores;
    - DCP8: 24.8 → 14.5 us (FP32: 14.3), and 32.2 → 19.0 us.
- GLM-5.3, TP4 DCP4 on one GB300 node, 60k-token prompts, 4 runs per variant on 2 nodes:
  - the selector goes from 21.0 to 14.2 us per call in decode (21 calls per step);
  - c1 TPOT p50 drops from 13.55 to 13.44 ms (-0.8%);
  - c2 TPOT p50 drops from 17.77 to 17.65 ms;
  - c8 ITL p50 drops from 19.30 to 19.13 ms.
- No behavior change:
  - The selection uses the same total order: score at the precision it was computed in, then the smaller token id.
  - Main and this PR select the same set:
    - in unit tests with forced boundary ties;
    - on 28.4M rows merged in GLM-5.3 runs and checked against main's selector. 97% of the rows with more than 2048 candidates had a tie at the boundary.
  - FP32 logits keep 32 score bits.
  - GSM8K is within run-to-run noise.

## Validation

### Serving: GLM-5.3 (`zai-org/GLM-5.3`, FP8)

Setup:
- TP4 + DCP4 on one GB300 node (4 GPUs), model runner V2, default DCP backend (`a2a`);
- `--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`;
- `--max-model-len 65536 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching`;
- `-cc.cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`: decode steps replay full CUDA graphs. With the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `main` itself did not start on this setup: the ranks diverged during PIECEWISE capture. That is unrelated to this PR.
- `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 60000 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos`, with 6 prompts at c1, 12 at c2 and 24 at c8.

Method:
- Two Slurm jobs on two nodes. Each job runs four servers on the same node: `main, PR, main, PR` and `PR, main, PR, main`.
- Values are the means over the 4 runs of each variant. The per-run spread of c1 TPOT p50 is 0.01-0.03 ms.
- `main` is 803bc13cf9.

| | c1 main | c1 this PR | c2 main | c2 this PR | c8 main | c8 this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT p50 (ms) | 13.55 | **13.44** | 17.77 | **17.65** | 52.52 | **51.91** |
| TPOT p99 (ms) | 13.65 | **13.47** | 20.65 | **20.46** | 61.50 | **61.07** |
| ITL p50 (ms) | 13.64 | **13.51** | 15.09 | **14.95** | 19.30 | **19.13** |
| TTFT p50 (ms) | 6673 | **6609** | 10059 | **9997** | 16284 | 16405 |
| output tok/s | 49.84 | **50.29** | 72.41 | **72.96** | 116.53 | **117.29** |

- Per run, c1 TPOT p50 is 13.55-13.56 ms on `main` and 13.43-13.46 ms with this PR.
- At c8, TPOT includes the steps that carry 8192-token prefill chunks of the other 60k-token prompts, so it varies by ±1 ms between runs. ITL p50 is the plain decode step: 19.23-19.42 ms on `main` and 19.04-19.21 ms with this PR.
- c8 TTFT depends on how the prefills interleave and is within its run-to-run spread (14.6-17.3 s).

GLM-5.3 has 21 sparse-indexer layers per step (`index_topk_freq=4`). Models with an indexer in every layer, like DeepSeek-V3.2, or DCP8 with 2x the candidates, save proportionally more per step.

### Kernel time in the model (torch profiler)

Same setup, 60k-token prompts, 8192 candidates per row (4 ranks × top-2048). The table gives the median per call on ranks 0 and 2 (they agree within 0.1 us). Each decode trace covers 29-40 steps (609-840 selector calls).

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| merge selector (`StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel`), decode c1 (1 row) | 19.4 us | **13.8 us** |
| merge selector, decode c8 (8 rows) | 21.0 us | **14.2 us** |
| merge selector per decode step (21 calls), c1 / c8 | 409 / 441 us | **290 / 298 us** |
| merge selector, first 8192-token prefill chunk (8192 rows) | 649 us | **449 us** |
| local top-k `cooperative_topk` (control), c1 / c8 | 9.6 / 9.9 us | 9.7 / 9.9 us |

The per-step saving (119 us at c1, 143 us at c8) matches the measured TPOT/ITL gain. The prefill-chunk saving is where the ~1% lower c1 TTFT comes from: every prefill chunk runs the merge in each of the 21 indexer layers.

### Microbenchmark

All-gather selector alone on one GB300, top-2048, ids drawn from a 64k context (16 id bits). us per call, CUDA graph of 100 launches. "Wide" scores are N(0, 3²). "Narrow" scores are 60 + N(0, 4²): they are more concentrated, so more of them tie at BF16 precision. "set == ref" checks the selection against an FP64 reference.

| DCP | rows | scores | main | this PR | set == ref |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| 4 | 1 | FP32 wide | 10.4 | **9.3** | yes |
| 4 | 1 | BF16 wide | 16.7 | **10.6** | yes |
| 4 | 1 | BF16 narrow | 21.0 | **11.5** | yes |
| 4 | 8 | BF16 narrow | 20.6 | **11.9** | yes |
| 8 | 1 | FP32 wide | 14.3 | **12.7** | yes |
| 8 | 1 | BF16 wide | 24.8 | **14.5** | yes |
| 8 | 1 | BF16 narrow | 32.2 | **19.0** | yes |
| 8 | 8 | BF16 narrow | 32.7 | **19.1** | yes |

FP32 logits keep 32 score bits and gain a little from the shorter id field.

### Correctness

- Selection on real model data:
  - A check-only build of this PR (not part of the diff) re-ran `main`'s selector (64-bit key) on the same gathered candidates after every DCP merge and compared the selected sets. It ran in eager mode, so it could sync.
  - Workload: GLM-5.3 TP4 DCP4, serving the greedy prompts below (up to 51k tokens), 200 GSM8K questions and 8 random 60k-token requests at c8. Prefill chunks and decode steps are both covered.
  - Two runs, counted on DCP rank 0: 28.4M merged rows.
    - 24.3M of them had more than 2048 valid candidates.
    - 23.7M (97%) had a tie at the top-k boundary.
    - **0 rows differed from `main`'s selection.**
  - The same check on GLM-5.3-Flash (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, kpool indexer, top-512 pools out of 2048 candidates), TP4 DCP4 with `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 64`, covered the long greedy prompts and 4 random 60k-token requests at c8.
    - It checked 4.65M rows: 4.45M had more than 512 candidates, and 4.23M had a tie at the boundary.
    - **0 mismatches.**
- GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions, 5-shot, completions, max concurrency 64), same setup as above:

| | runs | accuracy |
|---|---|---|
| main | 3 | 90.8, 91.4, 91.4 |
| this PR | 2 | 91.8, 91.6 |

- Greedy (`temperature=0`), sequential at c1, 38 prompts: 34 short ones (128 tokens each) and 4 real-text prompts of 8k, 20k, 38k and 51k tokens (256 tokens each). This setup is not deterministic run to run, even on `main`:
  - `main`, the same server queried twice: 11/38 and 16/38 outputs differ;
  - `main` across server restarts: 14/38 and 15/38;
  - this PR, the same server twice: 12/38;
  - this PR vs `main`: 11/38, 13/38 and 16/38.

  Most of the differing prompts are short ones. There every valid candidate is selected, so this PR cannot change their result. The outputs diverge after a common prefix, as numerical noise does. So greedy identity cannot separate the two here. The check on real model data above can.

### Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

| | this PR | main |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py` (GB300) | 117 passed (incl. 3 new) | 114 passed |
| `pre-commit` (ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, mypy, ...) | all hooks pass | |

New test `test_cutedsl_gathered_select_compact_keys_match_reference[16384|131072|1048576]`:
- BF16-valued scores: random, 64 distinct values (so the boundary tie spans hundreds of ids), all negative, padding mixed in, and all tied;
- token ids up to `num_positions - 1`;
- it checks that the default 64-bit key and the compact key (`score_bits=16`, `id_bits=dcp_topk_id_bits(num_positions)`) both select the FP64 reference set.

The server logs show no CuTeDSL JIT compilation during inference with this PR (`jit_monitor_mode=warn`), on GLM-5.3 and on GLM-5.3-Flash (kpool, `max_model_len // 4` id bits). So the new warm-up keys match the runtime keys.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- #61149 made the SM100 MQA logits (`fp8_fp4_mqa_logits`, `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits`) BF16. `sparse_attn_indexer` upcasts them (`as_fp32_logits`) whenever DCP is on.
- `StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel` builds `score_key << 32 | ~token_id` and runs up to 6 radix passes (11 bits each, the last one 9). It stops at the first pass whose threshold bin fits.
- With FP32 scores, the first 1-2 passes usually resolve the boundary. A BF16 score is complete after the first 16 key bits (passes 1-2), and it often ties at the boundary. The radix then continues:
  - pass 3 sees the 10 low score bits, which are all zero, plus the top id bit;
  - pass 4 sees id bits 30-20, which are constant because ids are below `max_model_len` (16 bits for a 64k context);
  - only passes 5-6 separate the tied candidates.
  - In the passes that separate nothing, every remaining candidate falls into one histogram bin, and the shared-memory atomics serialize on it.

**Fix.**
- `CompileKey` gains `score_bits` and `id_bits`.
- The key is `score_key >> (32 - score_bits)` followed by the low `id_bits` of `~token_id`, packed at the top of the 64-bit word. With BF16 logits and a 64k context, that is 32 bits and 3 passes.
- Padding keys stay 0 and still decode to -1.
- The order is unchanged:
  - the dropped score bits are zero for upcast BF16 values;
  - `~id & mask` preserves the order of ids below `2**id_bits`.
- `sparse_attn_indexer` (DSA) and the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer pass the following:
  - `score_bits=16` when the raw logits are BF16;
  - `id_bits` from `max_model_len`, or `max_pool_len` for kpool pool ids.
  - On a DCP rank whose prefill chunk is empty (no logits to inspect), `score_bits` follows the platform. That keeps it on the warmed-up key. 32 bits would also select correctly.
- Warm-up compiles the SM100 key: 16 score bits, and id bits for `max_model_len // index_kpool`.
- The last radix pass can now be narrower than the 512-thread block. For example, a 30-bit key gives passes of 11, 11 and 8 bits. The bin scan now covers whole block slices; bins at or above `num_bins` stay zero.

**Scope.**
- Only DCP > 1 with BF16 indexer logits (SM100) changes speed. FP32 logits keep 32 score bits.
- DCP = 1 does not run the merge.
- No new host syncs: `score_bits` comes from the logits dtype and the platform, and `id_bits` from `max_model_len`. All three are host-side metadata.
- No new CI step: the new test runs in the existing B200 "V1 Attention" step (`pytest v1/attention`), which has CuTeDSL.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` with "dcp topk", "top-k merge", "indexer dcp", "radix select bf16", "61149", "StableTopKFromGatheredCandidates", "dcp_indexer_cutedsl", "dcp top-k" and "sparse indexer bf16 logits" found no PR that changes the merge selector's key:
  - #47348 (CuTeDSL DCP top-k merge optimizations, before BF16 logits) and #50010 / #50366 (consumer-direct and owner-sharded top-k) restructure the exchange. They do not touch the key layout.
  - #63200, #62172 and #62240 make the local (non-DCP) top-k read BF16 logits. Under DCP, the upcast and this merge stay as they are.
  - #59367 bounds the merge's scratch memory and also edits `_merge_dcp_topk_global`. The changes are independent, and a rebase conflict would be trivial.
- No upstream issue covers it.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to investigate the regression, write the change and its test, and run the benchmarks and evals above. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the measurements.

** Not a blocker **

One thing on the benchmarks. They all use `max_model_len=65536`, which conveniently gives a 32-bit BF16 key that fits in 3 passes. At DSv4’s 1M you need 4 more. That pushes it to a 4th pass. 

I ran the selector alone on a sm100. At DCP8 that extra pass costs 1.5–4.7 µs, so the speedup can go from ~1.7× down to ~1.3×. At DCP4 I didn’t see a consistent difference. 

In any case, this PR is still faster in every config I tried and always picks the right tokens, so this _could be a follow-up_.

For (future) reference: roughly what I mean: pick the pass widths at compile time instead of fixed 11-bit passes:

```Python
max_bits = 12 if -(-used_bits // 12) < -(-used_bits // 11) else 11
num_passes = -(-used_bits // max_bits)
base, extra = divmod(used_bits, num_passes)
pass_bits = tuple(base + (i < extra) for i in range(num_passes))
# 32 -> (11,11,10), 34 -> (12,11,11), 36 -> (12,12,12), 48 -> (12,12,12,12)
```

then unroll the passes with `range_constexpr` (early exit on finished), size the histogram as `1 << max(pass_bits)`, and clear only the bins each pass scans.

detail.body:
## Overview

Since #61149 (DeepGEMM 2026-09-30), the SM100 MQA logits of the sparse indexer are BF16. Under DCP they are upcast to FP32 before the top-k, so the low 16 bits of every candidate score that reaches the DCP top-k merge are zero. The merge selector, `StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel`, radix-sorts the 64-bit key `score << 32 | ~token_id` in 11-bit passes. BF16 scores almost always tie at the top-k boundary. The radix then also walks the 16 zero score bits and the constant high bits of the token id, and each of those passes funnels every remaining candidate into a single histogram bin.

This PR packs only the bits that carry information into the key: the 16 high score bits when the logits were BF16, and the token-id bits that positions below `max_model_len` need. The selected set is unchanged.

## Claims

- Removes the DCP top-k merge cost that #61149 added. It applies to every DSA model with a sparse indexer under DCP on SM100 (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x).
  - With BF16 scores, the selector costs 1.6-1.7x what it costs with FP32 scores.
  - With this PR it is back to the FP32 cost. Per call at top-2048 on GB300:
    - DCP4: 16.7 → 10.6 us (FP32: 10.4), and 21.0 → 11.5 us on concentrated scores;
    - DCP8: 24.8 → 14.5 us (FP32: 14.3), and 32.2 → 19.0 us.
- GLM-5.3, TP4 DCP4 on one GB300 node, 60k-token prompts, 4 runs per variant on 2 nodes:
  - the selector goes from 21.0 to 14.2 us per call in decode (21 calls per step);
  - c1 TPOT p50 drops from 13.55 to 13.44 ms (-0.8%);
  - c2 TPOT p50 drops from 17.77 to 17.65 ms;
  - c8 ITL p50 drops from 19.30 to 19.13 ms.
- No behavior change:
  - The selection uses the same total order: score at the precision it was computed in, then the smaller token id.
  - Main and this PR select the same set:
    - in unit tests with forced boundary ties;
    - on 28.4M rows merged in GLM-5.3 runs and checked against main's selector. 97% of the rows with more than 2048 candidates had a tie at the boundary.
  - FP32 logits keep 32 score bits.
  - GSM8K is within run-to-run noise.

## Validation

### Serving: GLM-5.3 (`zai-org/GLM-5.3`, FP8)

Setup:
- TP4 + DCP4 on one GB300 node (4 GPUs), model runner V2, default DCP backend (`a2a`);
- `--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`;
- `--max-model-len 65536 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching`;
- `-cc.cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`: decode steps replay full CUDA graphs. With the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `main` itself did not start on this setup: the ranks diverged during PIECEWISE capture. That is unrelated to this PR.
- `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 60000 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos`, with 6 prompts at c1, 12 at c2 and 24 at c8.

Method:
- Two Slurm jobs on two nodes. Each job runs four servers on the same node: `main, PR, main, PR` and `PR, main, PR, main`.
- Values are the means over the 4 runs of each variant. The per-run spread of c1 TPOT p50 is 0.01-0.03 ms.
- `main` is 803bc13cf9.

| | c1 main | c1 this PR | c2 main | c2 this PR | c8 main | c8 this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT p50 (ms) | 13.55 | **13.44** | 17.77 | **17.65** | 52.52 | **51.91** |
| TPOT p99 (ms) | 13.65 | **13.47** | 20.65 | **20.46** | 61.50 | **61.07** |
| ITL p50 (ms) | 13.64 | **13.51** | 15.09 | **14.95** | 19.30 | **19.13** |
| TTFT p50 (ms) | 6673 | **6609** | 10059 | **9997** | 16284 | 16405 |
| output tok/s | 49.84 | **50.29** | 72.41 | **72.96** | 116.53 | **117.29** |

- Per run, c1 TPOT p50 is 13.55-13.56 ms on `main` and 13.43-13.46 ms with this PR.
- At c8, TPOT includes the steps that carry 8192-token prefill chunks of the other 60k-token prompts, so it varies by ±1 ms between runs. ITL p50 is the plain decode step: 19.23-19.42 ms on `main` and 19.04-19.21 ms with this PR.
- c8 TTFT depends on how the prefills interleave and is within its run-to-run spread (14.6-17.3 s).

GLM-5.3 has 21 sparse-indexer layers per step (`index_topk_freq=4`). Models with an indexer in every layer, like DeepSeek-V3.2, or DCP8 with 2x the candidates, save proportionally more per step.

### Kernel time in the model (torch profiler)

Same setup, 60k-token prompts, 8192 candidates per row (4 ranks × top-2048). The table gives the median per call on ranks 0 and 2 (they agree within 0.1 us). Each decode trace covers 29-40 steps (609-840 selector calls).

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| merge selector (`StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel`), decode c1 (1 row) | 19.4 us | **13.8 us** |
| merge selector, decode c8 (8 rows) | 21.0 us | **14.2 us** |
| merge selector per decode step (21 calls), c1 / c8 | 409 / 441 us | **290 / 298 us** |

### Microbenchmark

All-gather selector alone on one GB300, top-2048, ids drawn from a 64k context (16 id bits). us per call, CUDA graph of 100 launches. "Wide" scores are N(0, 3²). "Narrow" scores are 60 + N(0, 4²): they are more concentrated, so more of them tie at BF16 precision. "set == ref" checks the selection against an FP64 reference.

| DCP | rows | scores | main | this PR | set == ref |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| 4 | 1 | FP32 wide | 10.4 | **9.3** | yes |
| 4 | 1 | BF16 wide | 16.7 | **10.6** | yes |
| 4 | 1 | BF16 narrow | 21.0 | **11.5** | yes |
| 4 | 8 | BF16 narrow | 20.6 | **11.9** | yes |
| 8 | 1 | FP32 wide | 14.3 | **12.7** | yes |
| 8 | 1 | BF16 wide | 24.8 | **14.5** | yes |
| 8 | 1 | BF16 narrow | 32.2 | **19.0** | yes |
| 8 | 8 | BF16 narrow | 32.7 | **19.1** | yes |

FP32 logits keep 32 score bits and gain a little from the shorter id field.

### Correctness

- Selection on real model data:
  - A check-only build of this PR (not part of the diff) re-ran `main`'s selector (64-bit key) on the same gathered candidates after every DCP merge and compared the selected sets. It ran in eager mode, so it could sync.
  - Workload: GLM-5.3 TP4 DCP4, serving the greedy prompts below (up to 51k tokens), 200 GSM8K questions and 8 random 60k-token requests at c8. Prefill chunks and decode steps are both covered.
  - Two runs, counted on DCP rank 0: 28.4M merged rows.
    - 24.3M of them had more than 2048 valid candidates.
    - 23.7M (97%) had a tie at the top-k boundary.
    - **0 rows differed from `main`'s selection.**
  - The same check on GLM-5.3-Flash (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, kpool indexer, top-512 pools out of 2048 candidates), TP4 DCP4 with `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 64`, covered the long greedy prompts and 4 random 60k-token requests at c8.
    - It checked 4.65M rows: 4.45M had more than 512 candidates, and 4.23M had a tie at the boundary.
    - **0 mismatches.**
- GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions, 5-shot, completions, max concurrency 64), same setup as above:

| | runs | accuracy |
|---|---|---|
| main | 3 | 90.8, 91.4, 91.4 |
| this PR | 2 | 91.8, 91.6 |

- Greedy (`temperature=0`), sequential at c1, 38 prompts: 34 short ones (128 tokens each) and 4 real-text prompts of 8k, 20k, 38k and 51k tokens (256 tokens each). This setup is not deterministic run to run, even on `main`:
  - `main`, the same server queried twice: 11/38 and 16/38 outputs differ;
  - `main` across server restarts: 14/38 and 15/38;
  - this PR, the same server twice: 12/38;
  - this PR vs `main`: 11/38, 13/38 and 16/38.

  Most of the differing prompts are short ones. There every valid candidate is selected, so this PR cannot change their result. The outputs diverge after a common prefix, as numerical noise does. So greedy identity cannot separate the two here. The check on real model data above can.

### Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

| | this PR | main |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py` (GB300) | 117 passed (incl. 3 new) | 114 passed |
| `pre-commit` (ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, mypy, ...) | all hooks pass | |

New test `test_cutedsl_gathered_select_compact_keys_match_reference[16384|131072|1048576]`:
- BF16-valued scores: random, 64 distinct values (so the boundary tie spans hundreds of ids), all negative, padding mixed in, and all tied;
- token ids up to `num_positions - 1`;
- it checks that the default 64-bit key and the compact key (`score_bits=16`, `id_bits=dcp_topk_id_bits(num_positions)`) both select the FP64 reference set.

The server logs show no CuTeDSL JIT compilation during inference with this PR (`jit_monitor_mode=warn`), on GLM-5.3 and on GLM-5.3-Flash (kpool, `max_model_len // 4` id bits). So the new warm-up keys match the runtime keys.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- #61149 made the SM100 MQA logits (`fp8_fp4_mqa_logits`, `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits`) BF16. `sparse_attn_indexer` upcasts them (`as_fp32_logits`) whenever DCP is on.
- `StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel` builds `score_key << 32 | ~token_id` and runs up to 6 radix passes (11 bits each, the last one 9). It stops at the first pass whose threshold bin fits.
- With FP32 scores, the first 1-2 passes usually resolve the boundary. A BF16 score is complete after the first 16 key bits (passes 1-2), and it often ties at the boundary. The radix then continues:
  - pass 3 sees the 10 low score bits, which are all zero, plus the top id bit;
  - pass 4 sees id bits 30-20, which are constant because ids are below `max_model_len` (16 bits for a 64k context);
  - only passes 5-6 separate the tied candidates.
  - In the passes that separate nothing, every remaining candidate falls into one histogram bin, and the shared-memory atomics serialize on it.

**Fix.**
- `CompileKey` gains `score_bits` and `id_bits`.
- The key is `score_key >> (32 - score_bits)` followed by the low `id_bits` of `~token_id`, packed at the top of the 64-bit word. With BF16 logits and a 64k context, that is 32 bits and 3 passes.
- Padding keys stay 0 and still decode to -1.
- The order is unchanged:
  - the dropped score bits are zero for upcast BF16 values;
  - `~id & mask` preserves the order of ids below `2**id_bits`.
- `sparse_attn_indexer` (DSA) and the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer pass the following:
  - `score_bits=16` when the raw logits are BF16;
  - `id_bits` from `max_model_len`, or `max_pool_len` for kpool pool ids.
  - On a DCP rank whose prefill chunk is empty (no logits to inspect), `score_bits` follows the platform. That keeps it on the warmed-up key. 32 bits would also select correctly.
- Warm-up compiles the SM100 key: 16 score bits, and id bits for `max_model_len // index_kpool`.
- The last radix pass can now be narrower than the 512-thread block. For example, a 30-bit key gives passes of 11, 11 and 8 bits. The bin scan now covers whole block slices; bins at or above `num_bins` stay zero.

**Scope.**
- Only DCP > 1 with BF16 indexer logits (SM100) changes speed. FP32 logits keep 32 score bits.
- DCP = 1 does not run the merge.
- No new host syncs: `score_bits` comes from the logits dtype and the platform, and `id_bits` from `max_model_len`. All three are host-side metadata.
- No new CI step: the new test runs in the existing B200 "V1 Attention" step (`pytest v1/attention`), which has CuTeDSL.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` with "dcp topk", "top-k merge", "indexer dcp", "radix select bf16", "61149", "StableTopKFromGatheredCandidates", "dcp_indexer_cutedsl", "dcp top-k" and "sparse indexer bf16 logits" found no PR that changes the merge selector's key:
  - #47348 (CuTeDSL DCP top-k merge optimizations, before BF16 logits) and #50010 / #50366 (consumer-direct and owner-sharded top-k) restructure the exchange. They do not touch the key layout.
  - #63200, #62172 and #62240 make the local (non-DCP) top-k read BF16 logits. Under DCP, the upcast and this merge stay as they are.
  - #59367 bounds the merge's scratch memory and also edits `_merge_dcp_topk_global`. The changes are independent, and a rebase conflict would be trivial.
- No upstream issue covers it.

** Not a blocker **

One thing on the benchmarks. They all use `max_model_len=65536`, which conveniently gives a 32-bit BF16 key that fits in 3 passes. At DSv4’s 1M you need 4 more. That pushes it to a 4th pass. 

I ran the selector alone on a sm100. At DCP8 that extra pass costs 1.5–4.7 µs, so the speedup can go from ~1.7× down to ~1.3×. At DCP4 I didn’t see a consistent difference. 

In any case, this PR is still faster in every config I tried and always picks the right tokens, so this _could be a follow-up_.

For (future) reference: roughly what I mean: pick the pass widths at compile time instead of fixed 11-bit passes:

```Python
max_bits = 12 if -(-used_bits // 12) < -(-used_bits // 11) else 11
num_passes = -(-used_bits // max_bits)
base, extra = divmod(used_bits, num_passes)
pass_bits = tuple(base + (i < extra) for i in range(num_passes))
# 32 -> (11,11,10), 34 -> (12,11,11), 36 -> (12,12,12), 48 -> (12,12,12,12)
```

then unroll the passes with `range_constexpr` (early exit on finished), size the histogram as `1 << max(pass_bits)`, and clear only the bins each pass scans.

Rebased on main. Two upstream changes affect this PR:

- **#64580 (`indexer_logits_dtype`)**: BF16 indexer logits are now the default only for DeepSeek-V3.2/V4 on SM100. Other models, including GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash, default to FP32 again.

  - The microbenchmark is model-independent and unchanged. With FP32 logits the PR keeps 32 score bits and only shortens the id field (DCP4: 10.4 → 9.3 us, DCP8: 14.3 → 12.7 us).
- **#65178 (rank-major DCP gather)**: the selector now reads `[world, rows, topk, 2]` in place. The compact key is applied on top of that, and the new test builds the rank-major layout.

Change during the rebase: `score_bits` now comes from the configured `logits_dtype` (`dcp_topk_score_bits`), not from each rank's logits tensor or from the platform.
- Every DCP rank must key the merge the same way. Before, a rank with an empty prefill chunk fell back to a platform check, and so did warm-up.
- After #64580 that check would give 16 bits for an FP32 model on SM100 while the other ranks used 32.
- Now all ranks and warm-up derive it from the same config value.
